name: Hrudayangam Mehta
headline: PhD student in Computer Science
summary: I am a PhD student in Computer Science at Binghamton University, advised by Jeremy Blackburn, and a research assistant in the iDRAMA Lab. I work on AI applications in computational social science, preference optimization, and AI alignment. My published research covers language-model evaluation, vision-language reasoning, and human-robot interaction.

Compared prompting and decoding strategies, including Guided-CoT and self-consistency; analyzed classification errors and generated explanations.

bullets: Co-authored evaluations of GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet on floor-plan parsing and navigation action sequences.
Studied failures across map size, task complexity, and label density; co-inventor on the associated U.S. provisional patent application.

projects.name: Dialogue and planning for robotic guide dogs
bullets: Co-authored research connecting LLM dialogue with symbolic task planning and plan/scene verbalization.
Evaluated task specification on 77 simulated service requests; the multi-turn system achieved 94.8% accuracy.
